Inscribed with the seals of "Wang Wen Zhi" and "Scholar". According to the inscription of this picture, it is known that the painting was made when Wang Wen was studying in Wuxi Baojie Mountain in the year of Jiajing Wushen (the twenty-seventh year, 1548), and was made when the artist was 53 years old. The seal of appreciation is "Shiqu Baoji", "Qianlong Imperial Treasure", "Qianlong Appreciation", "Sanxitang Jingjian Seal " and "Yizi Sun". The lower right side of the painting is inscribed with a white square seal reading "Nothing to do with the green hills", while the lower left side of the painting is inscribed with a Zhu rectangular seal reading "Collected by Chen's Yuji of Leisure Stream".　　The painting must be a realistic view of the Baojie Mountain. In the house built halfway up the mountain, Wang Man is sitting sideways, reading to the scene, and the fishing boat is moored on the shore in front of the house, full of life. The artist uses strong ink to paint the miscellaneous trees in an unconventional manner, while the several huts are written in fine, light ink. The brushwork is thick and robust, and the contrast and contrast between light and heavy, thick and light, and static and dynamic are all appropriate. There are not many works by Wang Wen that have been handed down, so it is not easy to obtain this masterpiece in his prime.　　This painting was originally hidden in the Qing dynasty, but later fell into private hands and was purchased in Guangzhou in 1949 by Mr. Gu Tie Fu (1908-1990), an archaeologist at the National Palace Museum, whose family donated it to the National Palace Museum in 1994 in accordance with his wishes.
